nodes.text: Peace at the top of the road, traveler. This is the *Silver Shrine* — the mother-flame of every lamp in the Dawnlands. You've walked past a dozen of its children to stand here.
Warm yourself. Ask, if asking's why you climbed.

choices.text: Edda of the Last Lamp is your sister?
May I light a thought before the road?

nodes.text: Older than the city — the shepherds kept it on this shore before the first terrace was cut, a fire against the dark that never went out. Every road lamp from here to the ford was first lit from a wick carried down this hill. That's the whole faith, if faith's the word: _the dark is large, and we pass the light along._ Everything else is commentary.

My elder sister, and the family stubbornness went to her with interest. She took a wick down the mountain forty years ago and planted it at the worst mile of the road on purpose — 'the flame belongs where the dark is thickest, Sella, not where the view's nice.' She writes twice a year to check I haven't let the mother go out. Forty years. The mother-flame predates our family by centuries. I answer politely both times.

Then light it. ...There. The flame doesn't grant things — that's not its work. It *remembers you asked*, and it will be remembering all the way down the mountain, at every lamp you pass, in every window at dusk. Travelers tell me the road feels shorter afterward. I tell them that's the remembering, doing what remembering does.
Peace on your road. Pass the light along, in whatever coin you carry it.
